correctness.rationale: Exact identities for \(\sigma(2^a p)\) and \(\varphi(2^a p)\) reduce the target congruence to \(t=(3\cdot2^a-2)/(p-1)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) with \(t\equiv1\pmod{2^{a-1}}\). For \(a\ge3\), odd-divisor bounds leave only three candidates for \(t\). The candidates \(2^{a-1}+1\) and \(2^a+1\) would have to divide \(4\) or \(5\), respectively, which is impossible. Thus \(t=1\). For \(a=1,2\), explicit divisor checking yields exactly the exceptional pairs and the parametric pairs; direct substitution proves all converses. Finite tests corroborate only.
